3. Demand outlook

Peak demand in Goa grew from 540 MW in 2015 to 815 MW in 2023, an average
annual growth of 5.3 per cent. The Central Electricity Authority (CEA)
projects a peak of 1,180 MW by 2030 in its 20th Electric Power Survey. The
CEA figure assumes that hotel and residential loads grow faster than
industrial load, which has been flat since the closure of iron ore mines in
2012. Monthly peaks occur in May, when air-conditioning load is highest, and
in October, after the monsoon. The Electricity Department of Goa purchased
4,672 MU in 2022-23, of which about 79 per cent came from coal-based
central stations.

Table 3.1 summarises the projections. Scenario A assumes 5 per cent growth,
and Scenario B assumes 7 per cent growth. Under Scenario B, Goa would need
about 1,400 MW of firm capacity by 2030.
